purpose: silver.silver_flights holds one row per scheduled flight departing a New York area airport (EWR, JFK, LGA) in the first half of 2013, enriched with scheduled and actual departure/arrival times, delay and duration metrics, distance, aircraft registry attributes, and origin/destination airport reference data.
usage: Read the table at the grain of one row per (flight_date, carrier_code, flight_number). Consumers must handle nulls in dep_hhmm, dep_delay_minutes, arr_hhmm, arr_delay_minutes, and air_time_minutes for flights that did not complete as scheduled, and in the aircraft_* and dest_* reference columns where the underlying registry or airport lookup did not resolve a match.
limitations: The profile confirms whole-row uniqueness (duplicate_row_rate 0.0) but does not independently verify that (flight_date, carrier_code, flight_number) uniquely identifies a row; this grain is unverified until a deterministic measurement confirms it against the warehouse. aircraft_manufacturer, aircraft_model, aircraft_manufacture_year, aircraft_seat_count, and aircraft_engine_type are null for roughly 16-18% of rows where tail_number registry lookup failed. dest_airport_name, dest_municipality, dest_iso_region, dest_elevation_ft, and dest_longest_runway_ft are null for about 2.1% of rows where destination airport reference lookup failed. captured_at is retained as a pipeline load timestamp despite not being flagged is_airbyte_metadata in the profile; a reviewer should confirm its origin and whether it belongs in this contract at all.
